title: Nullable types: the safe call, the elvis operator, and the !! nobody should write

videos.script: In Java, any object can be null, and nothing tells you which. The compiler lets you call a method on nothing, and the phone finds out. {{types}} Kotlin splits every type in two. String, which is never null. And String with a question mark, which can be. You will see the compiler refuse both mistakes before anything runs. {{safe}} Then the four answers to one question: and if it is null? The safe call, which passes the null along. {{elvis}} The elvis operator, which replaces it with something you choose. {{smart}} The plain if, which the compiler remembers. {{bang}} And the double bang, which gives the crash back, and which you will learn to read as a warning. {{java}} Last, the border. Values from Java carry no question mark, and the protection stops there unless you put it back. By the end, the planner reads a number a student typed, and knows what to do when it is not a number.
